composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"

# Validate before Build so a missing or blank field is a 400 naming the offending
# fields, and the body is read (and republished) exactly once here.
validate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateOwnerFields
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: ensureUniqueIdentity

# Reject a create that would be a second member of an existing household (same deterministic
# householdId, keyed on lastName + postcode), responding 409 — unless 'sharesHousehold' is set,
# which declares the caller intends to join the household and bypasses this block.
ensureUniqueIdentity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureUniqueOwnerIdentity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: ensureCityCapacity

# Reject creating an owner when the request's city already contains 50 or more owners,
# responding 409.
ensureCityCapacity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureCityCapacity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: ensureDailyCreateLimit

# Reject creating an owner once 100 or more owners have already been created today
# (by registrationDate), responding 429.
ensureDailyCreateLimit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureDailyCreateLimit
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: build

build:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.BuildOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignCustomerCode

# postcode and HASH8 is the first 8 upper-hex chars of SHA-256(normalizedTelephone +
# lastName). A stable identity with no sequence number.
assignCustomerCode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerCustomerCode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHousehold

# Stamp the deterministic householdId (first 12 hex of SHA-256 of normalizedLastName|postcode)

assignHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerHousehold

  next: assignNamesakeCount

# (case-insensitive) and record it as namesakeCount before Save.
assignNamesakeCount:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerNamesakeCount
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save

save:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: audit

audit:

  next: warn

  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerBulkSignupWarning

  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond

  govern: [ transaction ]

          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'

          title: Address line 2

          maxLength: 255

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison

          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20

          minLength: 4
          maxLength: 4

          format: date

It only bypasses the duplicate block — the shared householdId is assigned automatically and deterministically regardless of this flag. A declared household member created this way is not flagged as a possible duplicate. Request-only override; never returned.

              readOnly: true

              title: Customer code
              description: The owner's customer code formatted '<REGION>-<HASH8>' where REGION is the region code derived from the owner's postcode and HASH8 is the first 8 upper-case hex characters of the SHA-256 digest over the normalized (E.164) telephone concatenated with the lastName.               format: int32
              minimum: 0
              maximum: 9

              readOnly: true

              example: 'NSW-1A2B3C4D-M26'

              type: string
              example: 'A1B2C3D4E5F6'
              readOnly: true

              readOnly: true
            membershipPoints:

              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 3
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: The owner's numeric membership level, from 1 to 4, derived from membershipPoints - level 1 for 0-1 points, 2 for 2-3 points, 3 for 4-5 points and 4 for 6 or more points.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 4

              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
